concept_uz: 1913-yil: Kembrijdagi matematik Xardi Hindistondan diplomi yoʻq hisobchining xatini ochadi — ichida yuzdan ortiq formula. Bu Ramanujan edi. Yillar oʻtib, kasalxonada Xardi «taksim raqami 1729 edi, zerikarli son» deydi. Ramanujan esa darhol javob beradi: bu juda qiziq son!

facts.claim: 1913-yil yanvarda Kembrijdagi Godfri Xardi Hindistondan xat oladi; muallif — Madrasdagi hisobchi, universitet diplomi yoʻq
Xatda 100 dan ortiq formula bor, koʻpi isbotsiz
Xardi avval tentaklik deb oʻyladi, qayta oʻqidi; bunday formulalarni topish uchun eng yuqori darajadagi matematik boʻlish kerak, deb yozgan
Ramanujan 1887-yilda Janubiy Hindistonda kambagʻal oilada tugʻilgan; matematikani asosan bitta eski qoʻllanmadan oʻrgangan, kashfiyotlarini daftarlarga yozgan
1914-yilda Kembrijga keldi; 1918-yilda Qirollik jamiyati aʼzosi boʻldi
Angliyada ogʻir kasal boʻldi; taksi 1729 voqeasini Xardining oʻzi yozib qoldirgan
1729 = 1³ + 12³ = 9³ + 10³ — ikki kub yigʻindisi sifatida ikki usulda yoziladigan eng kichik son (bugun skript bilan qayta tekshirildi)
Ramanujan 1920-yilda 32 yoshida vafot etdi; daftarlari bugun ham oʻrganilmoqda

style_line: Cinematic photoreal period drama, 1910s, 35mm film look, soft natural window light, warm amber and cool English grey tones, fine grain, respectful historical reconstruction. No text, no letters, no watermark.

refs.prompt: Vertical 9:16 interior of a small 1910s shipping office in Madras, South India: wooden desks with tall stacks of ledgers, a ceiling fan, tall green shuttered windows with hot golden sunlight, palm trees and a harbour crane visible outside. No people.

Vertical 9:16 full-body respectful reconstruction of a young South Indian man of about 25 in 1913, slim, short black hair, gentle deep-set dark eyes, a calm shy smile, a plain white high-collared shirt and a dark brown coat, white dhoti-style trousers, holding a THICK WORN BROWN LEATHER NOTEBOOK against his chest. Standing in warm light.

Vertical 9:16 full-body respectful reconstruction of a clean-shaven English mathematics professor of about 36 in 1913, slim, short neat light-brown hair, sharp thoughtful eyes, a grey tweed three-piece suit and a LONG RED-AND-WHITE STRIPED WOOL SCARF around his neck, standing upright.

Change the scene: the same man now sits at a wooden desk in an old Cambridge college study with tall leaded windows, oak bookshelves and a coal fire, holding open a long handwritten letter on thin paper covered with dense, blurred, illegible handwritten mathematical scribbles; he leans forward frowning. Grey morning light. Same face, same scarf, 9:16.

Combine the attached images: night in the same Madras office, a single oil lamp on the desk; the young man sits writing a long letter by hand, his thick worn brown leather notebook lying open beside the pages, moths around the lamp. Same face, same clothes, warm lamplight, 9:16.

Vertical 9:16 wide shot of a quiet Cambridge college court in 1914 on a grey, misty autumn morning: old pale stone buildings, a perfect green lawn, a gravel path, bare trees, a light cold drizzle. No people.

Vertical 9:16 street shot of a plain black 1910s London taxi cab with no visible markings or number plate stopped in front of a grey brick hospital entrance in winter; wet cobblestones, bare trees, cold blue light, a gas street lamp. No people.

Combine the attached images into one vertical 9:16 shot of a simple 1918 hospital room with a tall window and pale winter light: the young Indian man, thinner and tired, sits up in a white iron bed under a grey blanket with his worn brown leather notebook on his knees; the English professor in his grey tweed suit and red-and-white striped scarf has just come in, holding his hat, standing by the bed. Same faces, 9:16.

lines.text: Hindistondan xat? Yuzdan ortiq formula... birortasining isboti yoʻq!

scenes.prompt: Close push-in on the professor as he turns page after page of the letter faster and faster, his eyebrows rising; the coal fire crackles behind him. Audio: rustling paper, a crackling fire, a clock ticking. He says in Uzbek with a dry, precise English-accented male voice of about 36, sceptical: "Hindistondan xat? Yuzdan ortiq formula... birortasining isboti yo'q!" No subtitles, no on-screen text.

lines.text: Xat muallifi — Madrasdagi oddiy hisobchi. Universitet diplomi yoʻq.

scenes.prompt: The young man finishes the letter by lamplight, folds it carefully and looks at it with quiet hope; a moth circles the lamp. Slow push-in. lines.text: Matematikani u asosan bitta eski qoʻllanmadan oʻrgangan. Kashfiyotlarini daftarlarga yozib borgan.

scenes.prompt: Daytime in the hot office: the young man sits between the ledgers, secretly opens his thick worn brown leather notebook under the desk and fills a page with tiny blurred illegible handwriting, smiling to himself, glancing up so nobody sees. Audio: the ceiling fan, a ledger thumping shut, a pencil racing. An off-screen narrator says in Uzbek with a calm, warm middle-aged male storyteller voice: "Matematikani u asosan bitta eski qo'llanmadan o'rgangan. Kashfiyotlarini daftarlarga yozib borgan." lines.text: Avval tentaklik deb oʻyladim. Yoʻq... buni faqat eng buyuk matematik oʻylab topa oladi.

Audio: chair scraping, rain on the glass, a single low piano note. He says in Uzbek with a dry, precise English-accented male voice of about 36, quiet and amazed: "Avval tentaklik deb o'yladim. Yo'q... buni faqat eng buyuk matematik o'ylab topa oladi." No subtitles, no on-screen text.

lines.text: Bir yildan keyin Ramanujan Kembrijga keldi. Toʻrt yil oʻtib — Qirollik jamiyati aʼzosi!

scenes.prompt: The young man walks along the gravel path of the misty college court in his thin coat, hugging his worn brown notebook, looking up at the old stone buildings with wonder, shivering slightly in the drizzle. Slow tracking shot. Audio: footsteps on gravel, a distant chapel bell, rain. An off-screen narrator says proudly in Uzbek with a calm, warm middle-aged male storyteller voice: "Bir yildan keyin Ramanujan Kembrijga keldi. To'rt yil o'tib — Qirollik jamiyati a'zosi!" No subtitles, no on-screen text.

lines.text: Lekin sovuq iqlim uni yengdi — u ogʻir kasal boʻlib qoldi. Xardi uni koʻrgani taksida keldi.

scenes.prompt: The black taxi stops at the hospital; the professor in his grey tweed suit and red-and-white striped scarf steps out onto the wet cobblestones, glances back at the cab for a second, then hurries up the steps. Audio: an old engine idling, a car door, rain. An off-screen narrator says softly in Uzbek with a calm, warm middle-aged male storyteller voice: "Lekin sovuq iqlim uni yengdi — u og'ir kasal bo'lib qoldi. Xardi uni ko'rgani taksida keldi." No subtitles, no on-screen text.

lines.text: Taksimning raqami bir ming yetti yuz yigirma toʻqqiz edi. Juda zerikarli son.

scenes.prompt: The professor sits on a chair beside the bed, takes off his scarf and shrugs with a small bored sigh, trying to make light conversation; the young man in bed looks up from his notebook. Audio: a quiet ward, a ticking radiator. The professor says in Uzbek with a dry, precise English-accented male voice of about 36, bored and offhand: "Taksimning raqami bir ming yetti yuz yigirma to'qqiz edi. Juda zerikarli son." No subtitles, no on-screen text.

lines.text: Yoʻq, bu juda qiziq son! Ikki kubning yigʻindisi sifatida ikki xil yoziladigan eng kichik son.

scenes.prompt: Close-up: the young man's tired face suddenly lights up, his eyes sparkling, and he leans forward with a warm smile, tapping his notebook; the professor freezes, then laughs in disbelief. Audio: a soft magical chime, a surprised laugh. The young man says in Uzbek with a soft, gentle South-Indian-accented young male voice of about 30, instantly and joyfully: "Yo'q, bu juda qiziq son! Ikki kubning yig'indisi sifatida ikki xil yoziladigan eng kichik son." No subtitles, no on-screen text.

lines.text: Bir kub qoʻshuv oʻn ikki kub. Toʻqqiz kub qoʻshuv oʻn kub. Tekshirib koʻring — izohda yozing!

scenes.prompt: Slow pull-back from the two men smiling at each other over the open notebook, out through the tall window into the falling snow, holding on the lit window at the end. Audio: gentle piano, snow hush. An off-screen narrator says warmly, inviting the viewer, in Uzbek with a calm, warm middle-aged male storyteller voice: "Bir kub qo'shuv o'n ikki kub.
